target.statement: Mean AUC Price of Monotonicity (%) for German Credit (Statlog) across the three libraries (reported as 0.3% in Table 6)
target.table_ref: Table 6 (Dataset-level summary of PoM, AUC, German Credit row)

compute.basis: German Credit is tiny (700/300 rows, 20 features) but the protocol requires 3 libraries x 2 regimes x 625-combination grid search with 3-fold CV plus 1,000 paired bootstrap replicates; the grid search dominates and is CPU-bound, so a few hours on 8 cores is realistic if the repo's configs run as-is.

blockers: Repo may not contain exact grid definitions/constraint lists matching Appendix A (partial release)
Grid search of 625 configs x 3 folds x 3 libraries x 2 regimes is the main cost; exact reproduction of the 0.3% mean requires matching hyperparameter grids and seeds
Small dataset means PoM values are noisy; matching the reported mean to 0.1% may be sensitive to library versions
title: What's the Price of Monotonicity? A Multi-Dataset Benchmark of Monotone-Constrained Gradient Boosting for Credit PD
